courses.subject: DDS
courses.title: Doctor of Dental Surgery Year 1 Spring Mega Course
courses.description: Second in a series of multiple-disciplinary educational experiences designed to ensure required competency levels as dictated by national accreditation standards. Outcomes include demonstrated competence in oral and maxillofacial pathology-II; clinical medicine-II; practice administration II; hospital dentistry; temporomandibular disorders; laser dentistry and professional ethics in health care.
courses.requirements: Successfully completion of UNLV DDS program year 1 summer and fall semester courses DDS 9240, 9251, 9340, and 9351 or by written prior approval of course directors.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Human Structure and Function, Part II
courses.description: Studies the disciplines of biochemistry, cell biology, general microanatomy, and physiology. Since form and function are interrelated, how the two are integrated as they are taken from the cell level through tissues and then to organ systems will be taught. Exposure to cellular and histologic structures of tissues and organs and the exploration of the relationship between structure and function will be discussed, along with the integrated homeostatic relationship of body systems. Special consideration is given to those areas specifically related to dentistry and oral health. Prerequisite: Biochemistry, or special permission from instructor.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Microbiological and Immunological Concepts Part II: Oral and Infectious Diseases
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamentals of virology, infectious diseases and elements of the immune response to common pathogens. Clinical case studies will be used to illustrate infectious processes in oral and systemic diseases, with emphasis on infections of or impact on the oral cavity. Retrovirology, with an emphasis on Human immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), and an overview of several opportunistic infections will also be covered.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Advanced Gross Anatomy and Neuroscience
courses.description: Advanced topics in human gross anatomy in the context of dentistry and patient care. Head and neck anatomy presented regionally with pathology considerations and clinical correlates. Neuroanatomy presented regionally with focus on common neural diseases and conditions.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Principles of Clinical Dentistry: Operative Dentistry Lecture
courses.description: Introduces the basic principles, philosophy, and techniques of Operative Dentistry (the restoration of single teeth). Preparation and restoration of teeth for Class I and II type restorations using dental amalgam and composite restorative materials will be taught. Taught concurrently with DEN 7121L (Lab component).

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Princ Clin Dent: Operative Dentistry Lab
courses.description: Introduces the basic principles, philosophy, and techniques of Operative Dentistry (the restoration of single teeth). Preparation and restoration of teeth for Class I and II type restorations using dental amalgam and composite restorative materials will be taught. Taught concurrently with DEN 7121 (Lecture component).

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Intro to Intraoral Panoramic Radiology
courses.description: Introduction to Intraoral and Panoramic Radiography is a lecture/laboratory course designed to introduce students to the basic physics of X-ray production, its biological effects on living system, characteristics of radiographic images and fundamentals of intraoral and panoramic radiography in dentistry.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Bas of Perio Instru, Preven, & Interven Lec
courses.description: Presents clinical aspects of periodontal care and clinical skills needed to interact with patients in preventive periodontal care. Participants will learn to scale, root plane and polish the coronal surfaces of teeth with hand and ultrasonic instruments. Taught concurrently with DEN 7136L (Lab component).

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Basics of Periodontal Instrumentation, Prevention, and Interventions Lab
courses.description:

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Health Care Financing & Public Health
courses.description: An introduction to public health systems and health care financing, with emphasis on oral health care delivery to populations. Topics include: fluoridation, health care policy and reform, oral health care delivery systems, and access to care.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Community Outreach: Pediatric Education
courses.description: Presents the principles and practice of dental health education. This external rotation provides experience in a public health care setting where participants will be trained in patient health promotion and disease prevention. A dental education program on selected topics will be devised and implemented.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Research and Professional Development II
courses.description: Integrates research and professional development by introducing concepts in problem-solving, research skills for use with the library, internet, and key reference works, methods of scholarly and journalistic writing with emphasis on critical thinking, persuasion and evaluation of data, life-long learning and professional growth skills that benefit from a research experience. The exposure to research allows participants to embrace evidence-based practices, appreciate and understand the benefits of quality improvement, and participate in research focusing on the American dental patient experience.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Advanced Clinical Anatomy
courses.description: Advanced topics in clinically oriented anatomy with an emphasis on dental pathological and neurological conditions.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Principles of Endodontics Lecture
courses.description: Provides the opportunity to demonstrate skill in access preparations, debridement of root canal system, cleansing and shaping procedures, obturation procedures, and interim restorative procedures.

courses.subject: DEN

courses.description: Provides the opportunity to demonstrate skill in access preparations, debridement of root canal system, cleansing and shaping procedures, obturation procedures, and interim restorative procedures.

courses.subject: DEN

courses.requirements: Admitted student in the dental school and in good standing

Taught concurrently with DEN 7233SL (Lab Component).

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Partial Removable Dental Prostheses (PRDPs) Lab
courses.description: Presents principles of diagnosis and planning treatment for partially and fully edentulous patients. Taught concurrently with DEN 7233S (Lecture Component).

courses.title: Simulated Comprehensive Care Lecture
courses.description: Integrates both didactic information relative to the use of hand pieces in patient care, operative dentistry, and fixed prosthodontics, coupled with preclinical experiences in comprehensive care for a simulated patient. Topics include: treatment planning, more complex restorations, best practices in documenting procedures. The emphasis will be on patient-centered care, supported by evidence-based dentistry. Taught concurrently with DEN 7241SL (Lab component).

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Simulated Comprehensive Care Lab
courses.description: This lab component to DEN 7241S provides hands-on experience with the simulated patient. Training devices (e.g., CAD/CAM, etc.) will be used to enhance the learning experience. Emphasis will be placed on time management and quality of care necessary for patient-centered care. Exposure to fabrication of in-office appliances (e.g., bleaching trays, mouth guards, provisional and restorative matrices, diagnostic cast, etc.) will also be experienced. Taught concurrently with DEN 7241S (Lecture component).

courses.subject: DEN

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology II
courses.description: Oral Pathology I and II are lecture-seminar offerings which have been designed as two successive one-semester progressions to maintain continuity in the sequencing of material. Knowledge of the etiology, epidemiology, pathophysiology, and histopathology of pathologic processes as they relate to examination, evaluation, treatment, and prognosis of the patient will be learned. The scope of pathology that affects the oral and maxillofacial region will be explored, including developmental anomalies; reactive, inflammatory, and infectious conditions; immunologic disorders; neoplasia; and oral manifestations of systemic and genetic diseases. Emphasis is placed on formulating differential diagnoses and clinical-pathological correlation.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Clinical Medicine II
courses.description: Provides experience in the evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment planning for patients of all ages. Comprehensive treatment plans based on systemic findings and patients considerations will be developed to help achieve maximum integration between the study of disease, the study of the patient, and the diagnostic and therapeutic processes in the oral health care setting.

courses.subject: DEN
courses.title: Tempromandibular Disorders

.

Introduction to concepts of interprofessional and collaborative practice in a patient-centered environment is included.

The Basic Dermatology Curriculum exists as a 2 week or 4 week rotation. Each is designed as a supplement to a clinical rotation. In the absence of clinical experience (ie, entirely distant learning), students will complete the 4 week rotation in 2 weeks time.
Each module is approximately 30 minutes long. In the condensed schedule (see below), there will be approximately 4-5 modules each day. Therefore, students will have ample time to study the materials and seek out additional resources.
On the last day of the rotation, the students will attend an online interactive session with a dermatologist. The content of this session is at the discretion of the preceptor, which may include:
The preceptor will discuss a topic of interest.
Students will discuss any questions from the modules.
Students may be asked to make short presentations.
The dermatologist preceptor is available throughout the entire duration to give advice and answer questions.

courses.description: Students will learn the fundamentals of Emergency Medicine. This includes: triage, rapid evaluation, appropriate treatment plans, care coordination, and disposition. The student will participate in the direct evaluation, diagnosis, and management of patients admitted to the Emergency Department. Students will rotate through the Trauma, Pediatric, and Adult Emergency Department at UMC acting at a sub-intern level. Students will participate in several hours of medical student didactics and clinical workshops including EKG interpretation, ultrasound, and emergent airway management. Students will be participants for all procedures performed on their patients including IV insertion, wound management, incision and drainage of simple abscesses, bladder catheter insertion, nasogastric, and endotracheal tube insertion under direct supervision of attending and resident physicians. This rotation is specifically geared toward students interested in pursuing a career in Emergency Medicine.

The student will be immersed in an action-packed two weeks of wilderness activities and challenges in a variety of learning environments. The course will begin on Saturday and include three full days of rope and rescue training with the Las Vegas Search and Rescue Team, including a wilderness rescue scenario and evacuation. Students will be introduced to a variety of topics through didactics and specific challenges. Topics covered include Hypothermia, Submersion, Electrical Injuries, Bites, Stings, Edible and Poisonous Plants, and Heat-related Illness. Other activities scheduled for the clerkship include maps and orienteering, trips to Death Valley and Zion National Parks, desert survival workshop, and high altitude time on Mt. Charleston with avalanche training and rescue scenario. The two weeks will culminate with the SURVIVOR: Las Vegas Wilderness Medicine Challenge and Obstacle Course, which will test the student¿s wilderness medicine knowledge and skills.

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Longitudinal Interleaved Clerkship in Internal Medicine

courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: General Internal Medicine
courses.description: Students will be assigned to one of the four inpatient general ward teams. Sub-interns will function as PGY-ls on the Internal Medicine ward service, and will take call with their team (see syllabus for details). Days off and weekend coverage will be determined at the beginning of the rotation with other members of the team.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Cardiology / CCU Internal Medicine
courses.description: One hour of didactic teaching daily at the SIM Center, Room 3, at 7:00 a.m. Rounds on CCU/CIMC/Medical floors start after lecture and continue until done. Weekly guest lecture regarding various topics i.e.: pacemaker technology uses of amiodarone, interventional cardiology, peripheral vascular disease. Consult student will break from rounds when consult obtained and present to attending at the end of rounds. Teaching EKG reading during first two weeks of month when University is reading UMC EKGs. Viewing of all cardiac catheterizations on patients on the service daily. Review specific echograms on interesting patients as necessary. Each student will be given a topic in cardiology at the beginning of the rotation and will make a presentation on that topic at the end of the rotation. Attendance at cardiology outpatient clinic once during rotation.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Endocrinology Internal Medicine
courses.description: The student will gain experience in evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of disorders related to endocrinology and metabolism. The student will act as a team member on both outpatient and inpatient consultations. This will allow the student to see a number of patients at various stages of their disease as well as monitoring the progress of the disease and treatment.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Cardiology
courses.description: One hour of didactic teaching daily at the SIM Center, Room 3, at 7:00 a.m. Rounds on Medical floors start after lecture and continue until done. courses.title: Gastroenterology & Hepatology Internal Medicine

courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Infectious Disease Internal Medicine
courses.description: The student is expected to do all the infectious disease consultations requested and to follow these patients with daily examinations and appropriate handwritten notes. Emphasis is placed on differential diagnosis and therapy. Attention will be given to basic pathophysiology and laboratory diagnosis. There is a one-on-one relationship with the attending subspecialist. Literature review is considered an important part of the training and the student is expected to do mini reports. Infectious diseases encompass many areas of medicine and, by this fact, the student will have an in-depth experience of medicine.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Rheumatology Internal Medicine
courses.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the diagnosis and treatment of rheumatic diseases in an outpatient setting, including interpretation of laboratory tests and musculoskeletal imaging. Observation and active participation in history and physical examination techniques, with emphasis on areas unique to this specialty. The attending physician will supervise, mentor, and evaluate the student in these areas. Didactic sessions will occur with the attendings in the clinic setting. Students will be expected to read on a daily basis and prepare brief presentations with a written summary on areas of interest to them once per week.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Pulmonary Internal Medicine
courses.description: Didactic lectures given several times weekly. Daily rounds with attending physician including seeing patients in the hospital and outpatient clinic. Specific reading assignments with oral presentations and discussions. Review patients test results and write notes on patients daily. Student will be expected to follow and care for assigned patients. Students will be expected to do necessary assigned reading to expand their knowledge base on diseases encountered during their pulmonary elective. Attendance will be expected at ambulatory clinics.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Nephrology Internal Medicine
courses.description: Renal disorders are commonly evaluated by general internists. Disorders may be primarily renal in origin or systemic diseases that have profound secondary effects on the kidney, such as diabetes, vasculitides and atherosclerosis. General internists must be able to recognize, evaluate and initiate treatment for common renal disorders as well as understand the relationship between systemic processes and the kidney. Prevention of renal disease assumes paramount importance in decreasing the burden of chronic kidney disease. Occupational exposures in the dialysis unit to bloodborne pathogens such as Hepatitis B and C and HIV are discussed. Caring for chronic renal patients involves occupational risks to the practitioner. The socioeconomic aspect of chronic kidney disease on overall health care spending is important for students to understand. Environmental, nosocomial iatrogenic causes of renal disease are considered including the use of contrast dye, drug induced renal disease and medication induced changes in initiating renal hemodynamics and drug disposition. The difficult ethical issues of withholding renal replacement therapy and discontinuing renal replacement therapy are encountered.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Palliative Care Internal Medicine
courses.description: Palliative Care is an interdisciplinary team approach to improve the quality of life and relieve suffering for patients and families who face serious illness. The primary goal of the four-week Palliative Care clerkship is to treat the patient as a whole by addressing their physical, emotional, psychological, social, spiritual, and cultural needs. This is accomplished by exploring healthcare goals, assisting with medical decision-making, developing individualized care plans, providing pain and symptom relief, and offering spiritual, cultural, and psychosocial support. The Palliative Care team works alongside the Primary Care team to provide these services. Palliative Care is appropriate at any stage of illness, from the time of diagnosis through the end of life and bereavement. It can be provided in conjunction with curative and life-prolonging treatments. During this rotation, under the supervision of the palliative care team, students will be providing inpatient palliative care consultation services to patients and families facing serious illness.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Pain Medicine Internal Medicine
courses.description: During the Pain Medicine rotation, students are exposed to a spectrum of pain syndromes. Clinical experience is gained in both acute and chronic pain. Students gather experience in the treatment of acute pain and chronic pain as they rotate in office-based outpatient pain management, inpatient pain, and the interventional procedural suites. The chronic inpatient experience encompasses adult-care chronic and cancer-pain settings. Students are exposed to multi-disciplinary therapeutic approaches that include behavioral modalities, functional rehabilitation, as well as oral analgesics, intravenous therapies, neuraxial and perineural drug infusions, and invasive modalities. The outpatient experience includes seeing patients with core faculty in a consultative capacity and exposure to a wide variety of interventional techniques utilizing ultrasound technology as well as conventional radiography. Students seeking additional exploration of Pain Management may elect to do additional rotations in Pain Management during which time the training focuses on increasing familiarity with complex conditions and advanced techniques in Pain Management.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM
courses.title: Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Internal Medicine

Student will be expected to assume primary responsibility of patients under the direction of a senior medical resident. Students will be expected to do necessary assigned reading to expand their knowledge base on diseases encountered during their ICU elective. The student will act as a sub-intern completing daily rounds and admissions with their team. They will have at least 1 weekend day off each week.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: INTM

Under the supervision of an attending, fellow, and other faculty members, students gain hands-on experience diagnosing and treating benign and malignant tumors and hematologic conditions, as well as provide assistance with patient consults. Educational opportunities also include grand rounds, research seminars, and oncology clinics.

All students should understand that High Value Care is not the same as Low Cost Care and should be able to explain why. All students should be able to identify some form of waste in the clinical setting around them and propose ways to help reduce this by limiting tests/interventions or any non-beneficial tasks related to it.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Constitutional Law I
courses.description: Examines judicial review, congressional power under the Commerce, Taxing, and Spending Clauses and section five of the Fourteenth Amendment; substantive due process rights; the role of the states and national government under the Tenth and EleventhAmendments; and Separation of Powers. Prerequisite: Majors only, consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Property
courses.description: The legal basis for recognizing property, including some or all of the following topics: the creation, acquisition and extent of property interests; estates and future interests; landlord-tenant relations; real estate transactions; easements and servitudes, and public regulation of private property.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: American Legal History
courses.description: Examination of major issues in American legal history such as the role of lawyers in society and the role of law in developing the economy as well as the development of American legal institutions. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Evidence
courses.description: Focuses on the Federal Rules of Evidence and the issues that arise out of their use. Provides understanding of the rules including both their theoretical basis and how they function in the courtroom. Addresses preparation and presentation of various kinds of evidence, including proof of writings; qualifications and examination of witnesses; privilege; opinion testimony; demonstrative, experimental, scientific evidence, determination of relevancy; application of the hearsay rule. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Advanced Legal Analysis and Writing
courses.description: Analysis and writing about complex legal problems. Interpretation of various authorities and use of various forms of legal reasoning, types of argument, and techniques for clear and effective writing. Prerequisites: LAW 505, LAW 515, majors only, consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Products Liability
courses.description: Analyzes the substantive law, underlying theory and policy, and practice of products liability ' liability for injuries by defective consumer products. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Professional Responsibility
courses.description: Examines the law governing lawyers, the rules that govern how members of the legal profession, including judges as well as lawyers, may or must behave. Sources of these rules are many ' the Constitution, statutes, procedural, evidentiary and court rules, and rules of professional conduct. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Criminal Law
courses.description: Introduction to criminal law with emphasis on principles of criminal liability. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Employment Discrimination Law
courses.description: Examines the law of employment discrimination, focusing on Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Civil Rights Act of 1991, the Age Discrimination Employment Act of 1967 and other federal and state statutes, case law and regulations protecting the civil rights of employees and job applicants. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Water Law
courses.description: Acquisition and exercise of private rights in water, public rights and environmental protection, water distribution organizations, interstate water allocation, and federal-state relations in water resource management. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Patents, Trademarks and Trade Secrets.
courses.description: Study of the law relating to the protection of literary, artistic, and musical material; copyright law, including publication, subjects protected, and extent of protection; aspects of unfair competition, and right of privacy. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Constitutional Law II
courses.description: Examines the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment and related topics and the First Amendment's Free Speech and Free Press Clauses. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Pretrial Litigation
courses.description: Hands-on experience of the pre-trial litigation process in the federal court system. Students act as lawyers in a simulated civil case, interviewing and counseling clients, conducting legal research, drafting pleading, engaging in discovery practice, settlement negotiations and pre-trial motion practice. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Community Property
courses.description: Examines the law dealing with the classification, management and distribution of property acquisition within the community property jurisdictions of the United States. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.
courses.requirements: LAW 521

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Remedies
courses.description: Explores what lawyers and courts do to help someone who has been, or is about to be, wronged. In-depth look at the four major categories of remedies: damages, coercive remedies, declaratory relief and restitution. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Wills, Trusts and Estates
courses.description: Examines intestate succession, family protection, execution of wills, will contests, will substitutes, creation of trusts, modification and termination of trusts, administration of estates and trusts. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Federal Courts
courses.description: Examines federal jurisdiction and the law of federal-state relations. Covers federal judicial powers, congressional allocation of jurisdiction, choice of law, district court jurisdiction, appellate review, civil judicial reform, 42 USC Section 1983, Implied Right of Action, 11th Amendment and Federal Habeas Corpus. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Conflict of Laws
courses.description: Focuses on the problem of choosing which jurisdiction's law should be applied to transactions, relationships, or events with contracts in more than one jurisdiction. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Labor Law
courses.description: Explores the employer-employee-union relationship, its historical and economic development and its modern statutory framework.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Entertainment Law
courses.description: Surveys a wide range of legal issues pertinent to live and recorded entertainment, including intellectual property rights, contract formation and breach, regulatory schemes, labor issues, and First Amendment considerations. Prerequisite: LAW 629.
courses.requirements: Corequisite LAW 629

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Criminal Procedure I
courses.description: Basic course in criminal procedure. Covers laws regulating daily interactions of police and public, including laws of search and seizure and of interrogations. Does not cover rights subsequent to interrogation. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Public Lands and Natural Resources Law
courses.description: Provides an introduction to federal public lands and natural resources law. Focuses on the laws and legal systems that govern the classification and use of the federally owned lands comprising a third of America and the vast majority of the West. Examines major resource areas, including: minerals, timber, range, wildlife, recreation, wilderness, and cultural resources. Explores the interplay between environmental, economic, cultural, social and political factors in managing national parks, forest, and the public domain. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Criminal Procedure II
courses.description: Covers law and practices between the time defendant is charged and final disposition and sentencing. Includes prosecutorial discretion, bail, plea bargaining right to counsel, due process, sentencing, and post-conviction review. Prerequisites: Majors only or completion of first year courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Domestic Violence and the Law
courses.description: Examines violence against women and others in intimate relationships and the ways in which the law impacts and is impacted by domestic violence. Explores the history and social context of domestic violence and the dynamics and dimensions of abusive relationships. Prerequisites: Majors only or completion of first year courses or consent of professor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Legal Drafting
courses.description: Drafting legal documents such as contracts, leases, wills, by-laws, and employment agreements. Recognizing the importance of determining the client's objectives, researching the relevant law, organizing the document effectively, and drafting with accuracy, clarity, brevity, and appropriate tone. Prerequisites: LAW 505, LAW 515; majors only; consent of instructor.
courses.requirements: LAW 505 and LAW 515

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: International Business Transactions
courses.description: Explores a wide range of legal problems involving international trade, licensing, and investment issues. Prerequisites: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Intellectual Property Licensing Practicum
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of intellectual property licensing agreements with emphasis on drafting techniques for licenses involving patents, copyrights, trademarks, databases, and/ or trade secrets. This course satisfies the third semester Lawyering Process requirement. Prerequisites: LAW 505, and LAW 515, LAW 621 or LAW 629.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: International Intellectual Property
courses.description: This course covers the principles, treaties and mechanisms that regulate intellectual property at the international level (particularly copyright, patents, trademarks and internet domain names) and surveys the differences in the intellectual property laws of various countries.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Sports Betting & Fantasy Sports
courses.description: Examines legal and regulatory challenges of the rapidly expanding sports wagering industry. May include federal and state laws, industry operations, regulatory controls, sports corruption, illegal wagering prevention, and issues related to fantasy sports and daily fantasy sports within the evolving legal landscape.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Tribal Law & Governance
courses.description: In-depth study of the laws and governance of American Indian Tribal Nations: Indigenous law, federal law basics, and research and legislative drafting skills relevant to tribal sovereignty and governance. May include tribal constitutions, judicial systems, intergovernmental relations, and tribal gaming.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Anti-Money Laundering in Gaming Law
courses.description: Overview of anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing frameworks: international stakeholders, comparative legal approaches, and practical compliance skills. Emphasizes regulatory requirements and challenges across jurisdictions, with a focus on the gaming and casino industries. Addresses the evolving nature of financial crimes and global enforcement efforts.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Trial Advocacy
courses.description: Students design, execute, and practice the lawyering tasks specifically associated with actual courtroom trials, including opening statements, direct examination, cross-examination, evidentiary objectives, and closing arguments. Students perform these tasks in the context of hypothetical cases. Prerequisites: Prior or concurrent enrollment in LAW 606 and LAW 515.
courses.requirements: LAW 606

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Society of Advocates
courses.description: Students participate in forensic competitions, such as moot court and trial practice, involving legal research and analysis and brief writing as well as oral arguments or other advanced lawyering tasks. Prerequisites: LAW 515, majors only; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Civil Discovery
courses.description: Fundamentals of civil litigation discovery, including planning and addressing discovery issues. Emphasizes drafting interrogatories, document requests, admissions, and conducting depositions as well as discovery strategically to prepare cases for trial or settlement negotiations.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Climate Law Practicum
courses.description: Develops practical legal skills to address climate change through collaborative projects. Focuses on climate science, law, policy research, and legislative drafting producing publishable work for climate law organizations with experts and peer feedback.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Employee Benefits
courses.description: Introduces the statutory and regulatory framework of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA), with emphasis on fiduciary duties, reporting and disclosure, prohibited transactions, enforcement, and remedies. May include plan qualification, ERISA litigation, health and welfare plans, multiemployer plans, and withdrawal liability.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Accounting & Finance for Lawyers
courses.description: Fundamental accounting and finance principles relevant to business law practice for those with little business background. Emphasizes basic key concepts, vocabulary, and rules used in financial and accounting contexts. May include financial statements, basic accounting methods, and core financial principles.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Indian Gaming Law
courses.description: Explores legal and policy framework of Indian gaming, focusing on the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act of 1988, tribal sovereignty, and intergovernmental relations. May include regulatory jurisdiction, tribal-state compacts, revenue-sharing agreements, and contemporary legal and policy challenges related to tribal economic development through gaming.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Law, Morality, & Ethics in Film
courses.description: Examines the ethical responsibilities of lawyers as guardians of the rule of law. Studies vital role of ethics in preserving democracy and develop a commitment to leadership and positive societal change within the legal profession.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Opening Statements & Closing Arguments
courses.description: Focuses on developing skills to craft and deliver persuasive opening statements and closing arguments; practical application through performances and analysis of notable trials to enhance advocacy effectiveness. May include storytelling, courtroom communication strategies, and relevant legal principles.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Congressional Externship
courses.description: Explores the legislative process by placing students in legislative offices in Washington D.C. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Judicial Externship
courses.description: Explores the role of the judiciary in the legal system by means of in-class discussions and field placements in judicial chambers in federal and state courts in the state of Nevada. Prerequisite: Majors only, consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Legislative Externship
courses.description: Explores the state legislative process by placing students in the Legislative Counsel Bureau Office in Carson City and Las Vegas. Students are assigned to work with the Legislative Counsel Bureau, the House and Senate Judiciary Committees and interim committees. Prerequisite: Majors only or completion of first-year law courses or consent of instructor.
courses.requirements: Corequisite LAW 643

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Performance Tests on Bar Exams & in Practice
courses.description: Focuses on developing skills to complete bar exam performance tests and real-world legal writing tasks. May include legal analysis, statutory interpretation, fact evaluation, and drafting attorney work product. Emphasizes clarity, organization, sound judgment, and self-assessment in responding to unfamiliar legal issues under time constraints.
courses.requirements: LAW 505 and LAW 515

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Legislative Policy
courses.description: Simulates government affairs practice to explore the legislative process, statutory interpretation, and related legal issues. May include bill drafting, advocacy, policy analysis, and ethical challenges culminating in a mock panel.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Public Health Law
courses.description: Considers the role of law in shaping public health outcomes, balancing government authority and individual rights. Analytical and advocacy skills development relevant to public health law practice. May include legislation, regulation, and litigation on issues like vaccination, quarantine, and health infrastructure. Crosslisted with EGH 713.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Tenants Rights Residency
courses.description: Supervised practice representing tenants facing eviction in local Justice Courts. Centers on litigation skills, engaging in client advocacy, and exploring housing law and policy. May include access to justice, affordable housing, and the legal framework governing summary evictions in Nevada.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Cannabis Law & Policy
courses.description: Overview of Nevada¿s cannabis laws, policies, and regulatory framework, including the history of prohibition and legalization. Examines the interaction between state and federal law and encourages critical analysis of evolving cannabis policy issues through legal, regulatory, and enforcement considerations.
courses.requirements: LAW 603

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Law Journal
courses.description: Academic credit for successful completion of work by a member of the Nevada Law Journal. S/F grading only. Prerequisite: Successful completion of writing competition and selection by the instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Gaming Law Journal
courses.description: GAMING LAW JOURNAL

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Jury Voir Dire
courses.description: Focuses on jury selection, exploring the legal principles and psychology behind voir dire. May include techniques for jury questioning, use of strikes for cause and peremptory challenges, and strategies to assemble an optimal jury panel for trial.
courses.requirements: LAW 712

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Corporate Scandals Seminar
courses.description: Examines causes and consequences of corporate and legal scandals. Includes researching a unique scandal, in-depth analysis of what went wrong and proposing preventive strategies.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Government & Public Interest Externship
courses.description: Designed to provide experiential learning opportunities in a variety of public law agencies including the offices of the U.S. Attorney, Special Public Defender, Clark County District Attorney, Federal Defender, and others. Supervised fieldwork is coupled with a weekly seminar. Pre or Corequisite: Professional responsibility.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Community Law Practicum
courses.description: COMMUNITY LAW PRACTICUM

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Directed Readings
courses.description: Students earn credit for completing readings under the supervision and approval of a faculty member. Prerequisites: Majors only; consent of instructor required.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Students research and write about a legal topic of their choice under the guidance and supervision of a faculty member who has approved their choice of topic. Students further their knowledge of the area, as well as their legal research and writing skills. Prerequisite: Majors only, consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Parking Arbitration Practicum
courses.description: Introduces the legal framework, procedures, and role of arbitrators across various dispute contexts. Practices live case arbitrations with feedback to develop practical dispute resolution skills. May include arbitration in business, consumer, and court-connected settings. Eligibility restrictions may apply.
courses.requirements: LAW 517

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Evidence Skills
courses.description: Focus on using evidence in the courtroom with how the rules of evidence play out in the courtroom: advocacy skills rooted in understanding evidence, such as motions in limine, objections, and making a record for appeal. Will not examine aspects of trial advocacy that do not relate significantly to the rules of evidence.
courses.requirements: LAW 606

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Mediation Essentials
courses.description: Introduces mediation as a collaborative dispute resolution process. Preparation in mediation or apply mediation skills in legal and non-legal settings. May include communication techniques, emotional de-escalation, negotiation dynamics, ethical considerations, and mediation procedures.
courses.requirements: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Special Topics in Law
courses.description: Involves the study of a specialized topic in law that is not covered elsewhere in the law school curriculum. The particular topic will be announced during registration for the semester in which the course if offered. Prerequisites: Majors only or completion of first year law courses or consent of instructor. Crosslisted EGH 713, EGH 781

courses.subject: LDE
courses.title: Introduction to Leadership
courses.description: Introduction to leadership theories, concepts, and skills. Examination of the evolution of leadership theory; exploration of a personal leadership philosophy; understanding leadership as a process rather than a position; and analyzing the interaction of identity with leadership practice.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: LDE
courses.title: Leadership and Ethics
courses.description: Introduction to ethical decision-making and ethical leadership. Exploration of contemporary issues in organizations, communities, and society and the analysis of practices that encourage ethical behavior.
attributes: Online Education Online Fee Rate

courses.subject: LDE
courses.title: Leadership and Social Justice
courses.description: Examines how the leadership process can transform systemic social issues. Exploration of social change, activism, and advocating against social injustice; critical exploration of cultural identities; interrogation of systems of power, privilege, and oppression; and commitment to social justice.
courses.requirements: Minimum grade of C in LDE 201.
attributes: Online Education Online Fee Rate

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Foundations of Mathematics II
courses.description: Formalization, proofs, and models of quantificational logic; axiomatics; application to mathematical theories, including set theory. This course is crosslisted with MATH 452. Credit at the 600-level requires additional work.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Abstract Algebra II
courses.description: Sets, functions, groups, quotient groups, homomorphism theorems, Abelian groups, rings, polynomial rings, division rings, Euclidean domains, fields and vector spaces. This course is crosslisted with MATH 454. Credit at the 600-level requires additional work.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Introduction to Real Analysis II
courses.description: Topics include uniform continuity and fixed point theorems, sequences of continuous functions, approximation theorems, Riemann-Stieltjes integral, uniform convergence and infinite integrals, series of functions, differentiation in Rn. This course is crosslisted with MATH 458. Credit at the 600-level requires additional work.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Advanced Matrix Theory & Applications
courses.description: Rigorous mathematical treatment of orthogonal matrices, Gram-Schmidt method, Q-R factorization, least-squares fits, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, linear difference equations, systems of linear differential equations, unitary similarities, Schur's theorem, discrete Markov processes, power method, quadratic forms, singular value decompositions, pseudo-inverse, systems of linear inequalities, and simplex method. This course is crosslisted with MATH 463. Credit at the 600-level requires additional work.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Numerical Methods II
courses.description: Intermediate treatment of methods in computational linear algebra, numerical solutions of ordinary and partial differential equations, algorithmic design and analysis, and topics selected by the instructor. This course is crosslisted with MATH 467. Credit at the 600-level requires additional work.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: General Topology II
courses.description: Topological spaces, nets and filters, compactness, continuous functions, product and quotient spaces, introduction to algebraic topology. This course is crosslisted with MATH 484. Credit at the 600-level requires additional work.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: Method of separation of variables, Fourier series, divergence theorem and Green's identities, equations of mathematical physics, initial and initial boundary value problems, well-posedness, heat conduction in a thin rod, vibrations of a string, Laplace's equation, solution of the Dirichlet problem for a disc and for a rectangle. The 600-level MAT and STA courses that are normally available for graduate credit are those numbered 650 or higher; the exceptions are MAT 680, which may be counted for graduate credit in an education degree program, and STA 691, STA 693, and STA 695, which may be counted for graduate credit in a biological sciences program. This course is crosslisted with MATH 488. Credit at the 600-level requires additional work.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: INDEPENDENT STUDY
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Foundations of Mathematics IV
courses.description: Selection from the following topics: model theory, recursive function theory, set theory, mathematics of metamathematics. Prerequisite: MAT 652.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Abstract Algebra IV
courses.description: Detailed study of the following algebraic structures: groups, rings and ideals, fields, modules, and Galois theory. Prerequisite: A year of undergraduate abstract algebra or consent of instructor.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Real Analysis II
courses.description: Theory of measure, integration and differentiation: Banach spaces; Hilbert spaces; spaces of continuous functions. Prerequisite: MAT 658.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Integrative Mathematical Topics
courses.description: Survey of mathematical topics in an integrative manner. The topics may cover theory and applications in long stretches including probability and statistics; combinatorics, number theory and algebra; geometry and topology; ODE and PDE; computation and numerical analysis; Real and complex analysis. Prerequisites: At least nine credits at 600-level as required in Requirement #1.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Partial Differential Equations II
courses.description: Develops a functional analytical framework which will give students a deeper understanding of the subject matter. Topics include Sobolev and Holder spaces, embedding inequalities, weak solutions, regularity and maximum principles. Prerequisites: MAT 708 and MAT 729, or consent of instructor.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Topics in Numerical Analysis
courses.description: Topics selected by the instructor. May be repeated for credit with the consent of the mathematics department. Except under special circumstances, total credits limited to six. Prerequisite: MAT 765-766.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Library work and reports on topics of mathematical interest. May be repeated for credit with the consent of the mathematics department. Except under special circumstances, total credits will be limited to six.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Research, analysis, and writing towards completion of thesis and subsequent defense. May be repeated but only six credits will be applied to the student's program. S/F grading only.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Teaching Concentration Professional Paper Research
courses.description: Individual research towards an applied professional paper under the direction of a faculty member. May be repeated any number of times, but no more than three credits will count towards degree requirements. S/F grading only. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.requirements: Class unavailable to students who have not submitted immunization records or to students who have accepted online-only agreements.

The rotation presents greater exposure to ways of practicing community-based healthcare as well as important information about the policies, regulating agencies, and public health issues that impact access to care in Nevada communities. This rotation builds upon public health, special populations, and epidemiological concepts and issues discussed and raised in the longitudinal Nevada Community Service courses presented in Phase 1 of the curriculum. During these four weeks, students will work in the community for four full days, and one day per week will be led by faculty in reading review, small group discussions, and field trips relating to relevant policy, agency and public health concerns. courses.description: Foundational knowledge to clinical skills for normal and pathologic conditions associated with reproductive organs. courses.subject: OBGY
courses.title: General Obstetrics & Gynecology

At the completion of this rotation, the student should be able to list the elements of the OB/GYN annual examination with specific reference to preventative health care.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: OBGY
courses.title: Labor and Delivery Obstetrics and Gynecology
courses.description: The goal of the Labor & Delivery sub-internship is to learn how to efficiently diagnose, evaluate, and manage both common and unusual labor conditions in the inpatient setting. Students assume primary patient care responsibility for all patients admitted to the sub-intern service under the supervision of the chief attending. This clinical experience studies the relationship of clinical factors during pregnancy, labor, and delivery. Emphasis is placed on normal and abnormal conditions of pregnancy, labor, and delivery. The student functions on an intern-level and takes part in activities with house staff and faculty in the inpatient and outpatient arenas. The student is expected to participate in all facets of inpatient service. Attendance is expected at all lectures, conferences, and meetings which their team attends. Department conferences include morning rounds, attending rounds, grand rounds, and monthly journal club/teaching conferences.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: OBGY
courses.title: Women's Health Obstetrics & Gynecology
courses.description: The Women's Health sub-internship is designed to provide fourth-year students with experience in women's health over a life-time. Students learn the unique aspects of women's health spanning life stages; including adolescence, pregnancy, and annual health maintenance. Students work directly with physicians and nurse practitioners in an outpatient setting dedicated to teaching and high-quality patient care. Students interested in women's health will have an additional advantage of enhancing clinical and technical skills in preparation for advances residency training. This clinical experience is out-patient only. Didactic teaching consists of conferences, rounds, and assigned readings. Research opportunities are available for the interested student.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: OBGY
courses.title: Reproductive Endocrinology (REI) Obstetrics and Gynecology
courses.description: This sub-internship experience, in partnership with The Fertility Center of Las Vegas, is designed to offer students interested in an OB/Gyn career experience in a reproductive endocrinology (REI) setting dedicated to teaching and high-quality patient care. Students receive exposure to ultrasound, genetics testing, the management of human reproductive endocrine function, Advanced Reproductive Technologies (ART), and are introduced to disruptions in physiology and function, which can lead to endocrinological and infertility disorders. In addition to clinical requirements in the office and hospital, students will have the opportunity to attend a REI division conference. Common problems seen in REI include female and male infertility, recurrent pregnancy loss, polycystic ovarian syndrome, anovulation, amenorrhea, endometriosis, chronic pelvic pain, abnormal uterine bleeding, and uterine leiomyomas.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: OBGY
courses.title: Family Planning Obstetrics & Gynecology
courses.description: This two-week or four-week elective provides hands-on experience in family planning throughout diverse clinical settings. Family planning clinics provide resources that enable couples to determine whether, when, and how often to have children (with special consideration to birth spacing and maternal and child health). Students are exposed to contraceptive counseling and options counseling (i.e. abortion, adoption, parenthood). Contraceptive counseling and care includes insertion of long-acting reversible contraceptive methods (e.g. LARC, IUDs and implants). In addition, students will participate in first trimester ultrasound, medical and surgical abortions, medical and surgical management of early pregnancy failures, and intrauterine fetal demise. Clinical settings include outpatient visits and Operating Room (OR) experience.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: OBGY
courses.title: Patient Safety Obstetrics & Gynecology
courses.description: Students will understand and appreciate the vision of best possible health. Patient safety is making patient care continually safer by reducing harm and preventable mortality. The primary goal of this elective is to expose students to the unique multi-disciplinary field of patient safety, and to value patient safety as a global mission affecting all health care disciplines and settings. Students can expect to gain valuable experience and knowledge of patient safety and health care systems while they earn an IHI Quality and Safety basic certificate.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: OBGY
courses.title: Benign Gynecology Obstetrics & Gynecology
courses.description: This four-week sub-internship experience is intended for fourth-year medical students interested in pursuing OB/GYN as a career. During the experience, students will gain the knowledge and skills to evaluate and manage various gynecologic conditions within a multitude of settings: inpatient and outpatient service, and the Emergency Room (ER) and Operating Room (OR). Students will be closely supervised as they take on clinical responsibilities and demonstrate knowledge and values expected of an intern. During the sub-internship, students are responsible for hospital rounds, hospitalized and outpatient patients, preoperative workups, surgeries, involvement in gynecologic ultrasound and colposcopy, family planning services and procedures, and weekend call. Attendance at all service and departmental rounds and conferences are required to further knowledge and experience in OB/GYN.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: OBGY
courses.title: Maternal Fetal Medicine (MFM) Obstetrics & Gynecology
courses.description:
The sub-internship in maternal-fetal medicine is designed to provide a fourth-year student with experience in complicated pregnancy management. Students committed to a career in obstetrics and gynecology will enhance their clinical and technical skills in preparation for advanced residency training. Students work directly with house staff, sonographers, and Maternal-Fetal Medicine faculty within an atmosphere dedicated to teaching and high quality patient care. Students are considered members of the high-risk pregnancy team at both teaching hospitals, UMC and Sunrise Medical Center, as well as at the perinatal centers: UNLV Medicine OB/Gyn Maternal Fetal Medicine Clinic and Sunrise Hospital. Students will learn and apply principles involved with the management of medical and surgical complications associated with pregnancy, along with the management of structural, genetic, and physiologic fetal disease states. Additionally, students are exposed to basic and advanced obstetrical ultrasound, fetal surveillance techniques, the Doppler ultrasound, fetal echocardiography, amniocentesis, and invasive fetal procedures. At the end of the rotation, students will be able to identify
perinatal risk factors and have an appreciation for the medical and technical aspects of complex pregnancy management. This clinical experience includes inpatient, consultative, and outpatient complex pregnancy management. Experience in ambulatory care will take place in the high-risk pregnancy clinics housed in the perinatal centers. Didactic teaching will consist of conferences, teaching rounds, and selected readings.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

It is designed for students interested in gaining additional knowledge about orthopedic surgery and/or students wishing to become orthopedic surgeons. courses.subject: PBH
courses.title: Global Health
courses.description: This course introduces the principal health problems of the world's populations, and the major challenges to improving health at a global level. It is an inter-disciplinary exploration of the factors that account for these health patterns, ranging from their physiological basis to their economic, social and political context. Topics include: infectious diseases, injuries, risk factors, health system performance, and the role of international agencies in shaping the landscape of global health policy. Throughout the course, a heavy emphasis is placed on what we know and how we know about global health problems.

courses.subject: PBH
courses.title: Built Environment and Health
courses.description: This course will examine the built environment and its impact on health and discuss sustainable solutions with an emphasis on public health. The US and other nations are facing increasingly lethal and costly epidemics of acute and chronic diseases related to land use and built environment decisions. While the hazards presented by air and water pollution are well recognized there is only now increasing recognition of the hazards presented by building and community designs that fail to recognize human health. Built environment and health issues range from motor vehicle trauma to obesity, cancer, heart disease and are based on economic, financial, insurance, housing and other factors. This class will focus on environmental health, health threats of the built environment and creating healthy built environments.
courses.requirements: ENV 101 and PBH 205.

It serves as an introduction to quantitative, qualitative, mixed method and participatory approaches to research, as well as ethical issues in conducting research. Through the mix of texts, articles from the public health literature, and course work, students will build skills for conducting research and evaluation in public health.

courses.description: This course provides an introduction to biostatistical concepts and reasoning and provides a survey of data and data types. Specific topics include tools for describing central tendency and variability in data; methods for performing inference on population means and proportions via sample data; statistical hypothesis testing and its application to group comparisons; issues of power and sample size in study designs; and random sample and other study types. While there are some formulae and computational elements to the course, the emphasis is on interpretation and concepts.

courses.description: This course will examine the public health benefits of active transport and physical activity and concepts relevant to the built environment that facilitate or hinder participation in active transport and physical activity. Students will acquire knowledge of radiological procedures available, prepare patients for tests, explain the indications and limitations in the use of imaging equipment (including CT scans, ultrasound, radio nuclear techniques and angiographies), as well as identify the side effects and complications of invasive studies and contrast media (such as the hazards of radiation). courses.subject: REHB
courses.title: Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation (PMR) Internal Medicine
courses.description: PM&R is a branch of medicine which aims to prevent and limit impairment and disabilities and to enhance and restore functional ability and quality of life to those with physical impairments or disabilities caused by illness or injury. Students are exposed to the Comprehensive Integrated Inpatient Rehabilitation Program (CIIRP), an inpatient, interdisciplinary, acute-intensive rehabilitation program for survivors of serious injury or illness. Veterans are admitted with diverse medical and rehabilitation diagnoses with complex medical, neurological, orthopedic, and surgical conditions. The CIIRP offers students an interdisciplinary team approach to include the patient (Veteran) and his/her support system (family, caregiver, etc). Together, doctors, therapists, nurses, prosthetists, and other professionals work in unison with the patient to reach an optimal level of function and independence. (CIIRP services are provided by licensed and credentialed rehabilitation professionals including occupational therapists, physiatrists, prosthetists, psychologists, physical therapists, chaplains, nutritionists, nurses, orthotists, kinesiotherapists, speech language pathologists, social workers, recreational therapists and others as needed. The Veteran is the most important member of the CIIRP Rehabilitation Team.)

courses.description: Clinical foundations to the care of surgical patients. Emphasis is placed on establishing a diagnosis, exposure to the pathophysiology of surgical diseases, participating in the treatment of surgical patients, and supporting patients before, during, and after surgery.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: SURG
courses.title: Cardiothoracic/Vascular/Transplant Surgery
courses.description: Students will work with faculty and private surgeons and will also be part of the UMC3 surgery resident team rotating on CVT. Students will participate in patient care in both inpatient and outpatient settings. Students will participate actively in the operating room, including organ procurements. Readings and scholarly discussions are expected.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: SURG
courses.title: Trauma Surgery
courses.description: The student functions as a sub-intern on the Trauma ICU or Trauma Activation service with general surgery residents and Acute Care Surgery fellows at University Medical Center (UMC). The interested student should discuss with the course director which service may best suit the student's needs. The student participates in departmental and service didactic sessions. This rotation is designed as hands on, intensive experience in all phases of critical care. Students will respond to trauma activation. Students will be assigned a call schedule and night call should be expected.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: SURG
courses.title: Burn Surgery
courses.description: Investigates the exposure to the pathophysiology and management of thermal burns, electrical burns, chemical burns, inhalation injuries, physics, and their relationship to morbidity and mortality and patient recovery in the pediatric and adult population.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: SURG
courses.title: General Surgery
courses.description: The student functions as a sub-intern on the general surgery service. The student is assigned to one of the surgery resident teams at University Medical Center. The student will function at an intern level and will share duties with other members of the team, including UNLV 3rd year medical students. The student participates in departmental didactic sessions, service clinic, and all phases of pre-operative, intra-operative and post-operative care. This rotation is designed as an intensive experience in all phases of clinical practice. The general surgery services consist of resident teams on surgical-oncology, colorectal, and emergency consults. Students should discuss with the course director, so the appropriate assignments can be made. Attendance at private office hours allows for one-on-one interaction with attending physicians.
courses.requirements: School of Medicine student in good standing

courses.subject: WMST
courses.title: Race, Gender & the Making of Modern Medicine
courses.description: Examines the structural development of modern medicine from 1500 to the present, focusing on the construction of marginalized racial and gender identities and their relationship to medical institutions. Topics include plantation medicine, midwifery, alternative healing traditions, the commodification of health, cultural depictions of disease, and reproductive justice. Cross listed with AAS 433D and HIST 433D.

courses.subject: WMST
courses.title: Chicana Feminism and Experience
courses.description: (Satisfies Multicultural Requirement.) Examines Chicana/Latina experiences as they intersect with race, class, gender, sexuality, and nation. Examines the work of Chicana/Latina writers, feminists, scholars, performers, artists, filmmakers, and activists. Focuses on issues such as immigration, labor, family, language, education, spirituality, identity, patriarchy, homophobia, and racism. Examination of social work practice with the elderly based on critical analysis of theories of the aging process. This course is crosslisted with WMST 673. Credit at the 600-level requires additional work.
